title: Senses and the Brain
seo_title: Grade 4 Senses Worksheets: How the Brain Processes Information and Responds
standard_text: Use a model to describe that animals receive different types of information through their senses, process the information in their brain, and respond to the information in different ways.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on senses and the brain (NGSS 4-LS1-2): the five senses, nerves, how the brain processes information, responses, memories and how animals use their senses. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Senses take in information; the brain decides how to respond.
key_sub: Information goes from a sense organ along nerves to the brain. The brain processes it and tells the body how to respond.
body_html:
How to think about it

Animals take in information with their senses: sight (eyes), hearing (ears), smell (nose), taste (tongue) and touch (skin). Messages travel along nerves to the brain. The brain processes the information and sends messages to the muscles, and the body responds.

The brain can also store information as memories. Memories help animals respond better next time.

Example

You smell smoke and tell an adult. What is the response?

Smoke is the information.

The nose takes it in; the brain processes it.

Answer: telling an adult

Example

Where are messages from the ears processed?

Ears send messages along nerves.

Answer: in the brain

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the sense organ decides what to do. The brain decides.
  • Putting the response before the brain gets the message.
  • Mixing up the information (a sound) with the sense organ (the ear).

faq.q: How do the senses and the brain work together?
faq.a: Sense organs take in information and send messages along nerves to the brain. The brain processes the messages and tells the muscles how to respond.
A response is what an animal does after its brain processes information, like running away from a loud noise.
Information stored as memories helps animals respond better later, like remembering that a stove is hot.
